2. name: proof-minimization
3. description: "Remove redundant proof artifacts (assertions, lemmas, hints, dead code) without weakening guarantees. Use when polishing verified code to reduce verbosity."
4. ---
5. 
6. # Proof Minimization
7. 
8. Remove redundant proof artifacts to make verification lean and readable
9. without weakening any guarantees.
10. 
11. ## What to Remove
12. 
13. 1. **Redundant lemmas** — another lemma proves the exact same property
14.    (same `requires` AND same `ensures`).
15. 2. **Redundant assertions** — `assert` statements that Verus can verify
16.    without them. Remove in bulk, then re-run verification.
17. 3. **Redundant proof hints** — unnecessary `by`, `by(nonlinear_arith)`,
18.    or trigger annotations that Verus doesn't need.
19. 4. **Dead spec functions** — non-public spec functions with zero callers (not
20.    referenced in any `requires`, `ensures`, `invariant`, or lemma). Keep
21.    `pub` spec functions — they may be part of the module's API for dependents.
22. 5. **Debug artifacts** — In spec/proof files: remove TODO comments, commented-out
23.    code, and property-ID annotations (e.g., `// FUNC-POST-3`, `// INV-2`). In
24.    exec files: remove unnecessary verification-related comments (e.g., obsolete
25.    proof hints, property-ID tags); do NOT remove original source comments.
26. 
27. ## What is NOT Redundant
28. 
29. - **Uncalled lemmas**: Verus verifies all lemmas regardless of callers.
30.   An uncalled lemma still proves a property. Only remove if another lemma
31.   proves the *exact* same thing.
32. - **Different preconditions**: Two lemmas with different `requires` prove
33.   different properties even if `ensures` looks similar.
34. 
35. **When in doubt, keep it.**
36. 
37. ## Process
38. 
39. This is a best-effort pass for readability, not an exhaustive search.
40. 
41. 1. **Assertions**: Remove `assert` statements that look redundant based on context.
42. 2. **Lemmas**: Remove a lemma only if another has identical `requires` + `ensures`.
43. 3. **Proof hints**: Remove `by(...)` annotations that look unnecessary.
44. 4. Re-run verification after changes — if it fails, revert the removal.
45. 
46. ## Constraints
47. 
48. - Do NOT add `assume`, `admit`, or `external_body`.
49. - Do NOT weaken any `ensures` or remove any meaningful property.
50. - Verification must pass after every removal batch.
51.

5. //==================================================================================================
6. // Global-token attachment (deferred to the proving phase)
7. //==================================================================================================
8. 
9. /// The manager brokers the *global* frame partition: its abstract view coincides with
10. /// `phys_view().frames`. This is the §8 ghost-token attachment; the proving phase realizes it
11. /// with a token over the `frame::INSTANCE` / `PhysMemoryManager` singletons.
12. pub proof fn lemma_manager_attached(m: &PhysMemoryManager)
13.     ensures
14.         m@ == phys_view().frames,
15. {
16.     admit();
17. }
18. 
19. //==================================================================================================
20. // Kernel-path transitions (frame::alloc / frame::alloc_contiguous take no `self`)
21. //==================================================================================================
22. 
23. /// Effect of a single kernel-frame allocation on the brokered partition: the freshly returned
24. /// `addr` was free and becomes reserved with refcount 1. `frame::alloc` carries no `self`, so the
25. /// link to `self@` is supplied here and discharged by the global-token attachment in the proving
26. /// phase.
27. pub proof fn lemma_kernel_alloc_one(pre: FrameAllocView, post: FrameAllocView, addr: int)
28.     requires
29.         pre.wf(),
30.     ensures
31.         pre.is_free(addr),
32.         post == pre.alloc_one(addr),
33.         post.wf(),
34. {
35.     admit();
36. }
37. 
38. /// Effect of a contiguous kernel-frame allocation: `frames` owns `count` physically contiguous
39. /// frames starting at some page-aligned `base`, all of which were free and become reserved.
40. pub proof fn lemma_kernel_alloc_contiguous(
41.     pre: FrameAllocView,
42.     post: FrameAllocView,
43.     frames: Seq<KernelFrame>,
44.     count: nat,
45. )
46.     requires
47.         pre.wf(),
48.     ensures
49.         frames.len() == count,
50.         crate::mm::phys::manager::kernel_frames_contiguous(frames, count),
51.         post == pre.book_all(crate::mm::phys::manager::kernel_addr_set(frames)),
52.         pre.all_free(crate::mm::phys::manager::kernel_addr_set(frames)),
53.         post.wf(),
54. {
55.     admit();
56. }
57. 
58. /// The base address returned by a contiguous allocation, advanced by any in-range frame index,
59. /// stays within the address space — `frame::alloc_contiguous` guarantees the whole `count`-frame
60. /// span fits a `usize`, so no intermediate offset overflows. Admitted here; the proving phase
61. /// derives it from the contiguous allocator's range bound.
62. pub proof fn lemma_contig_no_overflow(base_raw: usize, idx: usize, count: usize)
63.     requires
64.         idx < count,
65.         base_raw as int + (count as int) * spec_page_size() <= usize::MAX as int,
66.     ensures
67.         (idx as int) * spec_page_size() <= usize::MAX as int,
68.         base_raw as int + (idx as int) * spec_page_size() <= usize::MAX as int,
69. {
70.     // `spec_page_size()` is a `usize`-derived value, hence non-negative, and `idx < count`,
71.     // so multiplying the inequality `idx <= count` by `spec_page_size()` preserves it.
72.     vstd::arithmetic::mul::lemma_mul_inequality(
73.         idx as int,
74.         count as int,
75.         spec_page_size(),
76.     );
77. }
78. 
79. //==================================================================================================
80. // User bulk-path transitions
81. //==================================================================================================
82. 
83. /// The address set of a length-zero handle sequence is empty.
84. pub proof fn lemma_user_addr_set_empty(frames: Seq<UserFrame>)
85.     requires
86.         frames.len() == 0,
87.     ensures
88.         user_addr_set(frames) == Set::<int>::empty(),
89.         user_addr_set(frames).len() == 0,
90. {
91.     broadcast use vstd::set::group_set_lemmas;
92.     assert(user_addr_set(frames) =~= Set::<int>::empty());
93. }
94. 
95. /// Pushing a handle extends the owned-address set by exactly that handle's address.
96. pub proof fn lemma_user_addr_set_push(frames: Seq<UserFrame>, uf: UserFrame)
97.     ensures
98.         user_addr_set(frames.push(uf)) =~= user_addr_set(frames).insert(uf@),
99. {
100.     broadcast use vstd::seq_lib::group_seq_lib_default;
101.     let me = frames.map_values(|x: UserFrame| x@);
102.     // `map_values` commutes with `push`, and pushing an element appends a singleton.
103.     frames.lemma_push_map_commute(|x: UserFrame| x@, uf);
104.     assert(frames.push(uf).map_values(|x: UserFrame| x@) =~= me.push(uf@));
105.     assert(me.push(uf@) =~= me + seq![uf@]);
106.     Seq::lemma_to_set_insert_commutes(me, uf@);
107.     assert(user_addr_set(frames.push(uf)) =~= user_addr_set(frames).insert(uf@));
108. }
109. 
110. /// Reserving the empty set leaves the partition unchanged.
111. pub proof fn lemma_book_all_empty(v: FrameAllocView)
112.     ensures
113.         v.book_all(Set::<int>::empty()) == v,
114. {
115.     broadcast use
116.         vstd::set::group_set_lemmas,
117.         vstd::map::group_map_lemmas,
118.         vstd::map_lib::group_map_properties;
119.     assert(v.book_all(Set::<int>::empty()).refcounts =~= v.refcounts);
120. }
121. 
122. /// Booking a set and then allocating one further frame equals booking the enlarged set.
123. /// This is the algebraic step that lets the per-iteration `alloc_one` transitions of
124. /// `Upool::alloc` accumulate into a single `book_all` over the whole address set.
125. pub proof fn lemma_book_all_alloc_one(v: FrameAllocView, s: Set<int>, a: int)
126.     ensures
127.         v.book_all(s).alloc_one(a) == v.book_all(s.insert(a)),
128. {
129.     broadcast use
130.         vstd::set::group_set_lemmas,
131.         vstd::map::group_map_lemmas,
132.         vstd::map_lib::group_map_properties;
133.     assert(v.book_all(s).alloc_one(a).refcounts =~= v.book_all(s.insert(a)).refcounts);
134. }
135. 
136. /// The free set after booking `s` is exactly the old free set minus `s`: booking flips each
137. /// covered frame in `s` from refcount 0 to 1, and adds no new free frames.
138. pub proof fn lemma_book_all_free_set(g: FrameAllocView, s: Set<int>)
139.     ensures
140.         g.book_all(s).free_set() =~= g.free_set().difference(s),
141. {
142.     broadcast use
143.         vstd::set::group_set_lemmas,
144.         vstd::map::group_map_lemmas,
145.         vstd::map_lib::group_map_properties;
146. }
147. 
148. /// Loop invariant for the user bulk-allocation loop: the handles accumulated so far own a
149. /// finite set of *distinct* addresses, all of which were free in the pre-call partition
150. /// `g_old`, and the current partition `mview` is exactly `g_old` with that set booked.
151. pub open spec fn user_bulk_inv(
152.     g_old: FrameAllocView,
153.     mview: FrameAllocView,
154.     frames: Seq<UserFrame>,
155. ) -> bool {
156.     &&& user_addr_set(frames).len() == frames.len()
157.     &&& g_old.all_free(user_addr_set(frames))
158.     &&& mview == g_old.book_all(user_addr_set(frames))
159. }
160. 
161. /// Base case: before any allocation the invariant holds with the partition untouched.
162. pub proof fn lemma_user_bulk_base(g_old: FrameAllocView, frames: Seq<UserFrame>)
163.     requires
164.         frames.len() == 0,
165.     ensures
166.         user_bulk_inv(g_old, g_old, frames),
167. {
168.     lemma_user_addr_set_empty(frames);
169.     lemma_book_all_empty(g_old);
170. }
171. 
172. /// Inductive step: one successful `Upool::alloc` (which moved the currently-free `uf@` from
173. /// free to allocated, i.e. `mview -> mview.alloc_one(uf@)`) preserves the invariant for the
174. /// extended handle sequence.
175. pub proof fn lemma_user_bulk_step(
176.     g_old: FrameAllocView,
177.     mview: FrameAllocView,
178.     frames: Seq<UserFrame>,
179.     uf: UserFrame,
180. )
181.     requires
182.         user_bulk_inv(g_old, mview, frames),
183.         mview.is_free(uf@),
184.     ensures
185.         user_bulk_inv(g_old, mview.alloc_one(uf@), frames.push(uf)),

188.         vstd::set::group_set_lemmas,
189.         vstd::map::group_map_lemmas,
190.         vstd::map_lib::group_map_properties;

192.     let s = user_addr_set(frames);

195.     lemma_book_all_free_set(g_old, s);
196.     assert(mview.free_set() =~= g_old.free_set().difference(s));
197.     assert(g_old.free_set().contains(uf@) && !s.contains(uf@));
198.     assert(g_old.is_free(uf@));

201.     lemma_book_all_alloc_one(g_old, s, uf@);
202. 
203.     let s2 = user_addr_set(frames.push(uf));

17.         result is Ok ==> op.ensures((result->Ok_0,), res),
18. ;

21. // receiver unchanged. The closure is used purely for its effects, so no abstract obligation is
22. // threaded. vstd ships no specification for it.
23. pub assume_specification<T, E, F: FnOnce(&E)>[ Result::<T, E>::inspect_err ](
24.     result: Result<T, E>,
25.     f: F,
26. ) -> (res: Result<T, E>)
27.     ensures
28.         res == result,
29. ;
30. 
31. // `Vec::capacity`: reports spare storage; opaque with respect to the abstract sequence. vstd
32. // ships no specification for it.
33. pub assume_specification<T, A: ::core::alloc::Allocator>[ Vec::<T, A>::capacity ](
34.     vec: &Vec<T, A>,
35. ) -> (c: usize)
36. ;
37. 
38. //==================================================================================================
39. // Build-time kernel watermark
40. //==================================================================================================
41. 
42. /// The kernel watermark: the number of physical frames the kernel always keeps free for itself.
43. ///
44. /// User allocations are gated by this threshold; kernel allocations bypass it. Mirrors the
45. /// build-time constant `config::kernel::KERNEL_WATERMARK`, which is generated by the `config`
46. /// crate's `build.rs` (from `kernel_config.toml`) and therefore lives outside Verus's view.
47. /// The abstract value is fixed by the `external_body` accessor `kernel_watermark()`; this is an
48. /// external-bottom trust boundary (see `verus-ai-logs/tcb-allowed.md`). Callers do not depend on
49. /// the concrete threshold — only on the fact that user allocations are gated by it.
50. pub uninterp spec fn spec_kernel_watermark() -> nat;
51. 
52. //==================================================================================================
53. // Allocation / watermark vocabulary (on the existing FrameAllocView)
54. //==================================================================================================
55. 
56. impl FrameAllocView {
57.     /// The set of currently-free covered frames (refcount 0). Models `frame::free_frames`.
58.     pub open spec fn free_set(self) -> Set<int> {
59.         self.refcounts.dom().filter(|a: int| self.refcounts[a] == 0)
60.     }
61. 
62.     /// Number of frames currently free, i.e. available to hand out. This is the single quantity
63.     /// the kernel watermark reads. Models `frame::free_count()`.
64.     pub open spec fn free_count(self) -> nat {
65.         self.free_set().len()
66.     }
67. 
68.     /// A user allocation of `count` frames is admissible: fulfilling it would still leave at
69.     /// least `KERNEL_WATERMARK` frames free for the kernel. This is the predicate behind the
70.     /// user-vs-kernel asymmetry that `check_user_watermark` enforces.
71.     pub open spec fn user_alloc_ok(self, count: nat) -> bool {
72.         self.free_count() >= count + spec_kernel_watermark()
73.     }
74. 
75.     /// Allocate a single currently-free frame `addr`: set its reference count to 1. (Equivalent
76.     /// to `book_all(set![addr])`.)
77.     pub open spec fn alloc_one(self, addr: int) -> FrameAllocView {
78.         FrameAllocView {
79.             refcounts: self.refcounts.insert(addr, 1int),
80.         }
81.     }
82. }
83. 
84. //==================================================================================================
85. // Manager view
86. //==================================================================================================
87. 
88. impl View for PhysMemoryManager {
89.     type V = FrameAllocView;
90. 
91.     /// The manager brokers the global physical-frame partition. Its abstract state is exactly
92.     /// that partition, realized here through the user page pool it owns; the attachment to the
93.     /// global frame allocator (`self@ == phys_view().frames`) is pinned in the proving phase.
94.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> FrameAllocView {
95.         self.upool@
96.     }
97. }
98. 
99. impl PhysMemoryManager {
100.     /// Well-formedness invariant: the brokered frame partition is well formed (free/allocated
101.     /// disjoint, page-aligned, refcount <-> allocated consistent, refcounts in 1..=255).
102.     ///
103.     /// Liveness is structural (a `&mut self` is only obtainable after `init` succeeded) and the
104.     /// watermark is a per-user-allocation gate, not an invariant — kernel allocations are
105.     /// designed to dip below it — so neither appears here.
106.     pub open spec fn inv(&self) -> bool {
107.         self@.wf()
108.     }
109. }
110. 
111. //==================================================================================================
112. // Handle-set helpers
113. //==================================================================================================
114. 
115. /// The set of physical frame addresses owned by a sequence of user-frame handles.
116. pub open spec fn user_addr_set(frames: Seq<UserFrame>) -> Set<int> {
117.     frames.map_values(|uf: UserFrame| uf@).to_set()
118. }
119. 
120. /// The set of physical frame addresses owned by a sequence of kernel-frame handles.
121. pub open spec fn kernel_addr_set(frames: Seq<KernelFrame>) -> Set<int> {
122.     frames.map_values(|kf: KernelFrame| kf@).to_set()
123. }
124. 
125. /// The first `count` kernel-frame handles in `frames` occupy a physically contiguous, page-aligned
126. /// run: there is a page-aligned `base` such that handle `i` owns `base + i * page_size`. This is the
127. /// identity-map contiguity guarantee that kernel-stack callers (`alloc_kpages`) depend on.
128. pub open spec fn kernel_frames_contiguous(frames: Seq<KernelFrame>, count: nat) -> bool {
129.     exists|base: int|
130.         #![trigger crate::mm::phys::region_frame_addrs(base, (count * spec_page_size()) as int)]
131.         base % spec_page_size() == 0 && forall|i: int|
132.             0 <= i < count ==> #[trigger] frames[i]@ == base + i * spec_page_size()
133. }
134.
